content: Vonoprazan is indicated for use in combination with amoxicillin, or with both amoxicillin and clarithromycin, for the treatment of Helicobacter pylori infection. It is also indicated for the relief of heartburn associated with non-erosive gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) in adults, with a recommended dosage of 10 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks. The safety and efficacy of vonoprazan have not been fully established in all contexts. Vonoprazan can decrease the levels or effects of rilpivirine by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is contraindicated. Amobarbital, apalutamide, armodafinil, belzutifan, bexarotene, bosentan, butabarbital, butalbital, carbamazepine, cenobamate, dabrafenib, efavirenz, elagolix, encorafenib, enzalutamide, eslicarbazepine acetate, etravirine, fosphenytoin, ivosedinib, lorlatinib, lumacaftor/ivacaftor, mitapivat, mitotane, modafinil, nafcillin, pentobarbital, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone, rifabutin, rifampin, rifapentine, and St. John’s Wort can all decrease the levels or effects of vonoprazan by inducing hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions necessitate avoiding co-administration or using alternative drugs. Vonoprazan can decrease the levels or effects of atazanavir, dasatinib, erlotinib, nelfinavir, and itraconazole by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. For itraconazole, therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended, and administration should be separated by at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after vonoprazan. Vonoprazan can increase the levels or effects of alfentanil, carbamazepine, cilostazol, citalopram, clonidine, colchicine, cyclosporine, dihydroergotamine, disopyramide, ergotamine, ethosuximide, everolimus, fentanyl, midazolam, pacritinib, pimozide, quinidine, quinine, repaglinide, sirolimus, tacrolimus, theophylline, and triazolam by inhibiting hepatic or intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor, and caution is advised when co-administering with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Monitoring and dose adjustments may be necessary. Vonoprazan can decrease the levels or effects of clopidogrel by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism, potentially reducing the plasma concentrations of clopidogrel’s active metabolite and its platelet inhibition effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. Vonoprazan can decrease the levels or effects of various iron formulations, including ferric carboxymaltose, ferric citrate, ferric derisomaltose, ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferric pyrophosphate (dialysate and IV forms), ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, ferumoxytol, iron dextran complex, iron sucrose, and polysaccharide iron, by inhibiting GI absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents, and caution with monitoring is recommended. In summary, vonoprazan exhibits significant drug-drug interactions primarily through its effects on CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism and GI absorption. These interactions necessitate careful consideration of co-administration, dose adjustments, and close monitoring to ensure therapeutic efficacy and safety.
